chunks: Do not be like him who hopes for the next life without action, and delays repentance by lengthening desires,
who utters words like ascetics in this world but acts like those who are eager for it;
if he is allowed something from it he does not feel satisfied; if he is denied he is not content;
he is not grateful for what he gets and covets for increase in whatever remains with him;
he refrains others but not himself; he commands others for what he himself does not do;
he loves the virtuous but does not behave like them; he hates the vicious but himself is one of them;
he dislikes death because of the excess of his sins but adheres to that for which he is afraid of death.

key_terms.الرَّاغِبِينَ: the eager ones / those desiring worldly gain

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of spiritual hypocrisy and negligence in religious practice according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) critiques the phenomenon of 'long expectation' (Tul al-Amal), where individuals delay repentance by assuming they have ample time, resulting in a dissonance between their ascetic rhetoric and worldly greed. This passage serves as a diagnostic tool in Shia spirituality for identifying spiritual negligence, warning that mere verbal piety without consistent action leads to a state of inner contradiction and fear of death despite continued sinning.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Do not be like him who hopes for (bliss in) the next life without action, and delays repentance by lengthening desires, who utters words like ascetics in this world but acts like those who are eager for it; if he is allowed something from it he does not feel satisfied; if he is denied he is not content; he is not grateful for what he gets and covets for increase in whatever remains with him; he refrains others but not himself; he commands others for what he himself does not do; he loves the virtuous but does not behave like them; he hates the vicious but himself is one of them; he dislikes death because of the excess of his sins but adheres to that for which he is afraid of death.
